title: CISNE REUNION
full_story:
Tonight at the Cisne Reunion, in addition to Bingo from 7 to 9 pm, the pageants will take center stage.  There will be the Tiny Tot, Little Miss, Junior Miss, and Miss Cisne Reunion pageants.  There are 7 young ladies running for the Miss Cisne Reunion title currently held by Kaleya Porter.  There are also 7 running for the JR Miss title currently held by Myla Hearle.  There are 10 little girls running for the title of Little Miss, the current Little Miss is Maleah Lane.

Look for the WNOI/Clay County Country Swag-N-Wagon for your FREE WNOI & LeMond Chevrolet Chrysler Black Wayfarer Sunglasses (also known as Sheldon Shades) plus WNOI & Sherwin-Williams Sunglasses & Fairfield Save A Lot Patriotic Pops for the kids during the Cisne Reunion tonight.

Friday, in addition to Bingo from 7 to 9 pm, Jake Perry and Hayden Brown will take the stage in the park at 7 pm.

Saturday will begin with race day registration and a community breakfast at the Community Center.  Race day Registration begins at 6 am on stage in the square, and the breakfast is from 7 to 10 am.

The 1 mile Fun Run is set to begin at 7:30 am, with the 15th annual 5K Run, Walk to begin at 8 am.  Tractor Show setup is from 8 to 10 am.  Car show registration begins at 9 am with awards at 12:30 pm, and the tractor show is at 10:30.  Kids’ Games and a FFA Petting Zoo on the square will be from 10 to Noon.  There will be a kids pedal pull at Noon on the square.  The annual parade lineup is at 2 pm at the high school with the parade at 2:30 pm.  Bill Atwood will serve as master of ceremonies for the Cisne Reunion parade.

The Ashes will perform from 4 to 6 pm, bingo will run from 5 to 9 pm and the Reunion closes with a performance by Duke Boys on the main stage at 7 pm.

The Cisne Masonic Lodge is grilling their World Famous Pork Chops and brats.  The lodge is located under the shelter on the south side of the square.  Sales will be during lunches and evening events and all day Saturday.  This years Cisne Reunion event pays tribute to the Cisne High School Class of 1976 on their 50th reunion and the Class of 2001 on their 25th reunion.

title: CARLE HEALTH EXPANDING
full_story:
Carle Health is planning to break ground for the construction of a Carle Health Outpatient Service Olney this afternoon.

The $45 million expansion of Carle Health Richland Hospital will bring a specialty medical office building and an emergency department to the health campus.

According to a news release from Carle Health, the facility will bring specialty care closer to Olney, reducing wait times and creating a more accessible care experience for the community.

During the groundbreaking, Carle Health leaders, along with city and county officials, will gather to celebrate the milestone.  Officials will also speak on how this expansion will better serve the area.

The groundbreaking will take place at noon, on the southwest side of the Carle Richland Memorial Hospital campus.

title: FALL FISH SALE

title: JEFFERSON COUNTY DISASTER DECLARATION
full_story:
The US Small Business Administration has notified the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (IEMA OHS) that it has approved a disaster declaration for Jefferson County for damage in the June 21st storms.  Residents and business owners in the contiguous counties of Marion, Washington, Perry, Franklin, Hamilton, and Wayne Counties will also be eligible to apply for the SBA’s long-term, low-interest disaster loans.

A federal Disaster Loan Outreach Center opened yesterday at the United Way office at 716 Main Street in Mt. Vernon.  SBA representatives will help residents, businesses and nonprofit organizations apply for low-interest loans for damage caused by the storms and tornado.  Walk-ins are welcome.  The center will remain open through August 20th.

Homeowners can apply for up to $500,000 in low-interest SBA disaster loans to repair or replace damaged or destroyed real estate.  Homeowners or renters can apply for up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.  Businesses and not-for-profits can borrow up to $2 million for physical damages.  The deadline to apply for loans for physical damages is September 28th, and the deadline to apply for economic injury loans is April 29th, 2027.

For online applications, visit sba.gov/disaster.  Applicants may also call SBA’s Customer Service Center at (800) 659 2955 or email [email protected]. People who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability may dial 7 1 1 for relay services.

title: LAKE LAND PART TIME HONORS
full_story:
Lake Land College is proud to announce more than 700 part-time students who earned academic honors for the 2026 Spring semester.

To qualify for the President’s List, a student must have completed six to 11 credit hours in courses numbered 040 or higher per semester, excluding summer term, with a GPA of 3.8 – 4.0.  Local students making the Presidents List include Wyatt Barber and Macy Worthey both of Louisville, Jeremy Boehm and Lisa Smith both of Edgewood, and Tabitha Hamilton of Cisne.

To qualify for the Honor’s List, a student must have completed six to 11 hours in courses numbered 040 or higher per semester, excluding summer term, with a GPA of 3.5 – 3.64.  Making the Honors List locally was Kylee Reynolds of Noble.

title: DCFS TRANSPARENCY LAW SIGNED
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer sponsored legislation recently signed into law to strengthen transparency and accountability in Department of Children & Family Service (DCFS) investigations involving allegations of child abuse or neglect.

“DCFS has repeatedly failed Illinois children and families, and a lack of transparency only makes those failures worse,” said Senator Plummer.  “When the state makes a determination in a child abuse or neglect case, the people involved deserve clear answers about the allegations, the findings, and their right to challenge that decision.  Government should never hide behind confusing notices or a broken bureaucracy.”

House Bill 4242 amends the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act by requiring DCFS to include additional information in written notices of final determinations involving indicated findings of abuse or neglect.

Under the new law, notices must include a statement of the allegation and indicated finding, the length of time the finding will remain in the State Central Register, and information regarding the right to request an administrative appeal.  The notice must also explain the deadline and process for filing an appeal, as well as the right to request a copy of the relevant investigative file.

“When children’s safety and families’ rights are at stake, there is no room for vague explanations or bureaucratic runaround,” added Plummer.  “This law forces DCFS to provide clear information and creates another layer of accountability for an agency that desperately needs it.”

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, September 25th, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 am from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: FAFSA COMPLETION RATE
full_story:
Illinois has reported a record-high completion rate for the FAFSA in 2026.

According to a news release from the Governor’s office, Illinois has had its highest-ever completion rate for the FAFSA, which now ranks it second in the nation.  The release states that the governor’s education initiatives helped lead Illinois to where it is today.

Seven years ago, Pritzker signed the FAFSA mandate into law, requiring Illinois public high school students to complete a financial aid application or submit a waiver.  Last year, Pritzker signed legislation that requires public high schools in the state to have a designated point of contact for FAFSA as well as provide assistance on financial aid forms during school hours.

Governor Pritzker added that he is committed to helping high school students in the state with affording college and achieving success in their careers afterward.
